title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #4

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The kayamba is a shaker used mainly at the (1 mark)
   A. Kenyan highlands only
   B. North of Lake Victoria only
   C. Kenyan coast
   D. Northern desert only

2. In art, tone or value means (1 mark)
   A. how old it is
   B. how big it is
   C. how light or dark something is
   D. how loud it is

3. What can be used as the core of an improvised macramé ball? (1 mark)
   A. A glass bottle
   B. A large stone
   C. Crumpled paper or old cloth
   D. A metal nail

4. Which position takes the centre pass to start the game? (1 mark)
   A. GK
   B. GD
   C. C, Centre
   D. GS

5. What does giving with the ball mean? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing the ball away
   B. Bending the arms as the ball arrives to soften the catch
   C. Handing the ball to the umpire
   D. Kicking the ball

6. Which is true about netball skills? (1 mark)
   A. Only shooters need to catch
   B. Passing and catching are needed by every player
   C. Nobody needs to move
   D. Only the umpire needs to pass

7. On the colour wheel, orange sits between (1 mark)
   A. yellow and blue
   B. blue and green
   C. red and blue
   D. red and yellow

8. What is a palette? (1 mark)
   A. A type of paper
   B. A kind of brush
   C. A frame
   D. A surface for mixing paint

9. Which of these is a light tone of purple? (1 mark)
   A. Pure purple
   B. Purple mixed with white
   C. Purple mixed with black
   D. Purple mixed with brown

10. Which of these letters is a tall letter with an ascender? (1 mark)
   A. u
   B. n
   C. x
   D. t

11. What joins the stems of a pair of quavers? (1 mark)
   A. A rest
   B. A beam
   C. A rope
   D. A bar of soap

12. How long does a quaver rest last? (1 mark)
   A. Four beats
   B. Half a beat
   C. Two beats
   D. One beat

13. A pair of quavers together lasts (1 mark)
   A. one beat
   B. four beats
   C. half a beat
   D. two beats

14. When you see a crotchet rest, you should (1 mark)
   A. keep the beat but not clap
   B. clap twice
   C. shout
   D. stop the whole song

15. Which move is a step? (1 mark)
   A. d to m
   B. d to d
   C. m to d in one jump over r
   D. d to r

16. A coil of clay is (1 mark)
   A. a plate
   B. a long thin roll like a snake
   C. a flat sheet
   D. a hard brick

17. A slab of clay is (1 mark)
   A. a flat piece
   B. a round ball
   C. a hollow cup
   D. a thin roll

18. On the Kenyan flag, black stands for (1 mark)
   A. the land
   B. the sea
   C. the people of Kenya
   D. peace

19. How does gymnastics help the heart and lungs? (1 mark)
   A. It has no effect
   B. Moving the whole body makes the heart beat faster and stay strong
   C. It removes the lungs
   D. It stops the heart

20. Which health benefit comes from gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Better flexibility
   B. Weaker bones
   C. Less energy
   D. Slower breathing always

21. A song that is played fast has a (1 mark)
   A. low pitch
   B. soft dynamic
   C. long title
   D. fast tempo

22. Which folk songs welcome a new baby? (1 mark)
   A. Initiation songs
   B. Work songs
   C. Funeral songs
   D. Naming songs

23. To keep the camera steady you should (1 mark)
   A. hold it with both hands and keep elbows near your body
   B. shake it
   C. hold it at arm's length with one finger
   D. throw it

24. How should you hold a camera or tablet? (1 mark)
   A. Over your head
   B. With both hands
   C. By one corner
   D. By the lens

25. The screen of a camera (1 mark)
   A. is the strap
   B. shows what you will photograph and photos you have taken
   C. makes sound
   D. is the battery

26. Photography is (1 mark)
   A. the art of taking pictures with a camera
   B. painting with a brush
   C. cutting paper
   D. singing songs

27. Why should you not use very hot water on a plastic recorder? (1 mark)
   A. It makes it play higher
   B. It makes it louder
   C. It makes it heavier
   D. It can bend the plastic

28. On the staff, the note B sits on (1 mark)
   A. line 1
   B. line 3
   C. line 2
   D. line 5

29. What should you do before playing to prevent spreading germs? (1 mark)
   A. Eat sweets
   B. Share the recorder
   C. Chew gum
   D. Wash your hands

30. In a supine float, you lie (1 mark)
   A. on your back with ears in the water
   B. face down
   C. curled up
   D. standing

31. Water games help learners to (1 mark)
   A. feel comfortable in the water
   B. study more
   C. forget to swim
   D. avoid the pool

32. Why do we shower before entering the pool? (1 mark)
   A. To learn to float
   B. To warm the water
   C. To get dry
   D. To keep the pool clean

33. What helps your body to float? (1 mark)
   A. Kicking hard only
   B. Water pushes up on it and lungs full of air
   C. Holding a stone
   D. Being heavy

34. Which Kiswahili word means crab? (1 mark)
   A. mamba
   B. simba
   C. kaa
   D. chura

35. In the giraffe stretch, you (1 mark)
   A. crawl
   B. swim
   C. roll
   D. stand tall on toes with arms high

36. A hare hop suits a rhythm that is (1 mark)
   A. absent
   B. quick like ta-te ta-te
   C. silent
   D. very slow

37. A portfolio is (1 mark)
   A. a folder for keeping creative works together
   B. a song
   C. a ball
   D. a kind of paint

38. Which is a component of a folk song? (1 mark)
   A. Distance
   B. Weight
   C. Price
   D. Community of origin

39. The Kenya National Anthem is called (1 mark)
   A. Malaika
   B. Twinkle Twinkle Little Star
   C. Jambo Bwana
   D. Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu

40. Which material can you use to make a portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. Manila paper or cardboard
   B. Sand
   C. Glass
   D. Iron sheets

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Why is light important in photography? (2 marks)

42. Describe how to do the mushroom float. (3 marks)

43. Describe how to learn the East African Community anthem for performance. (4 marks)

44. What is a side roll? (2 marks)

45. Describe how to paint the Kenyan flag on paper. (5 marks)

46. Describe how you would enter the pool and perform a glide safely. (5 marks)

47. Explain the difference between the prone float and the supine float. (3 marks)

48. Why is it important to warm up before doing gymnastics? (3 marks)

49. Explain how to prepare and perform a folk song with your class. (5 marks)

50. Give three warm-up activities before sprinting. (3 marks)

51. What is a rest in music? (2 marks)

52. Why do we improvise a netball? (3 marks)

53. List the components of a folk song that you can analyse. (4 marks)

54. Explain why it is dangerous for a child to jump into a river to rescue someone. (3 marks)

55. Give three responsible ways of using a device for photography. (3 marks)

56. What does it mean to improvise a rhythmic pattern? (3 marks)

57. Explain the meaning of diction and why it matters. (3 marks)

58. Write what the signs p and f mean. (2 marks)

59. What is a montage? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Kenyan coast
   The kayamba is a coastal shaker used by the Mijikenda and other coastal people.

2. C — how light or dark something is
   Tone is the lightness or darkness of a colour or shading.

3. C — Crumpled paper or old cloth
   Paper or cloth makes a soft core that keeps its shape.

4. C — C, Centre
   The Centre takes the centre pass.

5. B — Bending the arms as the ball arrives to soften the catch
   Bending the arms takes the force out of the ball.

6. B — Passing and catching are needed by every player
   Every player passes and catches during a game.

7. D — red and yellow
   Orange is made from red and yellow, so it sits between them.

8. D — A surface for mixing paint
   A palette is where paints are mixed.

9. B — Purple mixed with white
   White makes a tint.

10. D — t
   The letter t is a tall letter, with a stem that rises above small letters.

11. B — A beam
   A thick line called a beam joins them.

12. B — Half a beat
   A quaver rest is half a beat of silence.

13. A — one beat
   Two half beats make one whole beat.

14. A — keep the beat but not clap
   A rest is a silent beat, and the beat continues.

15. D — d to r
   Doh to ray is to the next note.

16. B — a long thin roll like a snake
   A coil is a long, thin, even roll of clay.

17. A — a flat piece
   A slab is a flat sheet of clay.

18. C — the people of Kenya
   Black represents the people of Kenya.

19. B — Moving the whole body makes the heart beat faster and stay strong
   Active movement strengthens the heart and lungs.

20. A — Better flexibility
   Stretching and rolling help joints and muscles bend freely.

21. D — fast tempo
   Tempo is speed.

22. D — Naming songs
   Naming songs are sung when a baby is named.

23. A — hold it with both hands and keep elbows near your body
   A steady hold gives a sharp photograph.

24. B — With both hands
   Two hands prevent dropping.

25. B — shows what you will photograph and photos you have taken
   The screen displays the view and the saved pictures.

26. A — the art of taking pictures with a camera
   A photograph is a picture taken by a camera.

27. D — It can bend the plastic
   Heat can warp plastic.

28. B — line 3
   B is on the middle line.

29. D — Wash your hands
   Clean hands help hygiene.

30. A — on your back with ears in the water
   You look at the sky.

31. A — feel comfortable in the water
   They build confidence.

32. D — To keep the pool clean
   It removes dirt and sweat.

33. B — Water pushes up on it and lungs full of air
   Buoyancy and air in the lungs.

34. C — kaa
   Kaa is a crab.

35. D — stand tall on toes with arms high
   Reach up like a giraffe.

36. B — quick like ta-te ta-te
   Hares hop quickly.

37. A — a folder for keeping creative works together
   It protects and presents works.

38. D — Community of origin
   Components include community, type, message, participants and instruments.

39. D — Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu
   The Kiswahili title is Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu.

40. A — Manila paper or cardboard
   Manila paper folds easily.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Light lets the camera record the picture. With good light the subject is clear.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: In shallow water take a breath and put the face in. Bend the knees and hug them to the chest with the chin tucked. The back rises to the surface. Hold for a few seconds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to it several times, read and discuss the words, clap the rhythm, sing line by line and then sing the whole song together in unison while standing straight and respectful.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: A roll along the mat sideways with the body straight and long like a log.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sideways roll, 1 mark for the straight body.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Cut a rectangle of paper in the ratio three to two. Draw the stripes and the thin white lines lightly with a ruler. Sketch the shield and the crossed spears in the middle. Paint black at the top, red in the middle and green at the bottom, leaving the white lines. Let it dry and attach it to a stick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for the rectangle, drawing stripes, shield, colour order and drying with handle.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Get permission and warm up. Enter feet first by the steps or sit and slide. Stay in shallow water. Stand with the back to the wall and stretch the arms overhead. Put feet on the wall, breathe, put the face in, push off gently and glide with a straight body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five parts.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prone is face down in the water with arms stretched forward. Supine is on the back with the face up and ears in the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each float, 1 mark for the difference.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Warm-up prepares the muscles and joints, prevents injury and helps you perform better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Choose a song and say the community, type and message. Share roles among soloist, chorus and instrumentalists. Practise pitch, rhythm, tempo and dynamics. Add gestures and expressions. Perform with respect and take a bow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for choosing the song, roles, practising, expression and performing respectfully.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Jogging, arm circles, leg swings, gentle stretching, short easy strides. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: A sign for silence for a certain length of time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for silence, 1 mark for length of time.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Some schools do not have enough balls. We can use materials we have, such as string and waste cloth. It lets more learners practise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Community of origin, type or occasion, message, participants and their roles, and instruments.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct components.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: The child may also drown because water can be deep or fast. It is safer to shout for an adult and throw something that floats.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the danger, 2 marks for the safe action.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission before photographing someone; do not photograph in private places; do not share photographs without permission; use it only for the set task. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: To make up a pattern on the spot without writing it first, using an instrument such as a drum or shaker to keep to the beat of a song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for making up on the spot, 1 mark for no writing first, 1 mark for using an instrument.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Diction is saying the words clearly. It matters because the audience can understand the message of the song.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 2 marks for the reason.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: p means soft. f means loud.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: A picture made by joining many cut pictures or pieces of material on a background.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many pieces, 1 mark for joined on a background.
